title: Priority-sequenced fallbacks and lease-based shielding for private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Private and VPC deployments must tolerate control-plane upgrades and partial region failures without cascading tenant impact. Existing tactics (global quarantines, blunt throttles) either cause large availability windows for critical tenants or are too manual during rollouts.

Goal: Implement an automated, lease-based shielding mechanism together with a priority-sequenced fallback matrix and circuit-breaker profiles per-tenant. The system should allow: (1) short-lived capacity leases to pin tenant scheduling during control-plane churn, (2) an ordered set of graceful degradations (e.g., model variant degrade -> reduced concurrency -> region swap -> shed non-essential requests) applied by priority, and (3) deterministic circuit-breaker triggers driven by SLO budgets and real-time resource signals.

Success criteria: during a simulated region upgrade or SIGMA failover we keep high-priority tenant P95 latency within 2x baseline and error-rate below 1% without manual intervention; lower-priority tenants may experience planned degradations.

Why this is different: combines lease-based admission semantics (to prevent eviction storms during rolling upgrades) with an explicit, versioned fallback matrix per-tenant that preserves predictable SLAs for high-value customers while enabling safe automated load shedding for best-effort workloads.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Lease service implemented: tenants can request short-lived scheduling leases and the scheduler honours leases during control-plane upgrades.
2) Fallback matrix engine: ability to declare an ordered list of degradation steps per tenant and to push a rollout that exercises steps automatically based on signals.
3) Circuit-breaker profiles: thresholds defined by SLO budgets (latency, error-rate, cpu/gpu saturation) that flip states and trigger the next fallback step.
4) Canary run: execute a blue/green upgrade in a staging private cluster and demonstrate no >2x latency spike for priority==high tenants.
5) Runbook and playbook updated and validated by SRE and Solutions Eng.
6) End-to-end observability: per-tenant incident journal, metrics, and tracing to confirm behavior.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (POC): implement lease token service (token minting, renewal, revocation) and a shim in the admission controller to honour leases. Build a simple fallback library with three steps: MODEL_DEGRADE -> CONCURRENCY_LIMIT -> REGION_FAILOVER.
Phase 2 (integration): wire circuit-breaker state machine into the request router; define SLO-budget based thresholds and meaningful hysteresis. Add feature flag gating and config rollout via control-plane config-store.
Phase 3 (canary & validation): run multi-region failover scenario in staging with synthetic traffic and customer-seeded tenants. Collect metrics and iterate thresholds.
Phase 4 (rollout): gradual enabling across private deployments with per-account priority tiers and a migration script to backfill fallback matrices.

Key components to deliver: lease-service (k8s operator), admission-controller changes, router circuit-breaker integration, fallback engine, UI hooks in Console for priority and fallback inspection, runbooks and dashboards.
progress_updates: 2025-01-12: Spike complete; basic lease token prototype and gRPC API implemented. Observed no eviction during simulated control-plane restart on single-node cluster.

2025-01-25: Design review with PM (Lena Torres) and SRE (Marco Silva). Decided to store fallback matrices as versioned JSON in config-store and to use optimistic lease renewal to avoid thundering renewals.
2025-02-03: POC admission-controller shim landed in branch feat/lease-shielding. Unit tests + integration tests added. Awaiting security review for token auth mechanism.

2025-02-10: Circuit-breaker prototype integrated with router; initial thresholds based on P95 latency and GPU queue depth. Ran load test showing priority routing works but lower-priority eviction triggers too aggressively — need hysteresis tuning.

2025-02-18: Canary start in staging cluster: enabled for 3 test tenants (high/medium/low). High priority maintained latency within 1.6x; medium/low saw expected degradations. Logging and per-tenant journaling validated.
risks:
- Lease tokens introduce an extra control-plane surface; compromised tokens could lead to capacity misallocation. Mitigation: short TTLs, KMS-backed signing, auditable revocations.
- Incorrect thresholds could either shed too early or not protect high-priority tenants. Mitigation: gradual rollout, synthetic canaries, and automated rollback hooks.
- Complexity in the router/circuit-breaker increases maintenance burden. Mitigation: keep fallback engine small, well-documented, and configurable via Console.
- Cross-region data consistency for leases and fallback matrices may cause split-brain. Mitigation: use leader leases scoped per-region and a reconciliation job with safe defaults.
rollback_plan: Feature-flagged components with immediate disable. If canary shows regressions > acceptance criteria: - disable fallback engine -> return to existing admission behaviour; - revoke all active lease grants and fall back to normal scheduler; - trigger emergency rollback of router changes. Post-mortem to identify incorrect threshold or lease bug.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for lease lifecycle (mint/renew/revoke).
- Integration tests: admission-controller + scheduler honoring leases during rolling upgrades.
- Failure injection: control-plane restart, region partition, node OOM.
- Load tests with 3 tenant classes and monitoring of P50/P95/P99 latency and error-rate.
- Chaos runbook: simulate delayed lease renewal and ensure fallback matrix still protects priority tenants.
